C-01.note: 6-pt favor scale coded rating per spec example. Script flagged 'no' (gain: 'no people will be saved') vs 'nobody people will die' (loss) - token-list artifact, not the manipulation; negation_change judged 0.

C-02.note: 'winning nothing' -> 'losing $0.05' reframes the same $0.05 as gain(0) vs loss; number added.

C-04.note: 'the 150 people' -> '98% of the 150': a proportion token is added. 98% is a share of a fixed population, not an event probability - explicit_probability coded 0 (borderline; alternative coding 1).

C-05.note: Same borderline proportion logic as C-04 (95%).

C-06.note: Same borderline proportion logic as C-04 (98% of 500).

C-07.note: Same borderline proportion logic as C-04 (95% of 500).

C-08.note: Open 0-20 numeric entry - no fixed options, NaN. Card arm adds $50 / 50% / $3.00.

C-09.note: Buy (WTP) vs be-paid (WTA) assigns different respondent roles - role_change 1. Same 1-in-1,000 number both arms. Bracket scale, coded numerical_estimate.

C-11.note: Response options ARE the stimulus and change wholly.

C-12.note: self_other=other is a judgment call (statements are about Linda, a third party; the respondent gives own probability ratings). Probability scale is verbal-labeled 1-6, no explicit numerical probability -> 0.

C-13.note: Anchor 85 vs 1000 feet. Outcome is open numeric estimate -> NaN options (anchor MC has 2 options but is not the outcome item).

C-14.note: Anchor 12 vs 65 countries; same NaN rationale as C-13.

C-15.note: Evaluates the physician's decision -> other. 8%/2% and age 70/75 change. Outcome valence differs materially (success vs death), not equivalent consequences reframed -> gain_loss 0. 'did not succeed' -> 'succeeded' is a negation change.

C-16.note: In-group relationship flips (US car banned in Germany vs German car banned in the US) - role_change 1, borderline. '8 times more likely' is relative likelihood, not a probability -> 0.

C-17.note: Per-trial binary prediction (1/2, red/green) - reconciled from stage8 'numeric_estimate' (that referred to the aggregated share); stage5 n_options=2 supports binary. Composition numbers all change (7/3 cards vs 4/2 faces; 10 vs 6 trials).

C-19.note: Numerals constant; the change is number words ('one comes up 3, and two come up 6's' vs 'all three come up 6's'). Borderline: coded 0 per 'a number CHANGES' reading, noted. 11 fixed buckets A-K.

C-20.note: Question identical; hour brackets in response options shift up (numbers change in options).

C-21.note: Reciprocity question-order manipulation: us_second arms add the reciprocal North-Korea->UK question before the target. Target question identical; implemented as insertion, not pure reorder, so manipulation_location is kept.

C-22.note: 'allow' vs 'forbid'. 'forbid' is not on the negation token list -> negation_change 0.

C-23.note: Attributed source changes (Bin Laden vs Washington); quote and scale identical.

C-24.note: Induction paragraph differs (walk outdoors vs meeting a Muslim stranger); 1-9 intention items identical.

C-25.note: Judges the permissibility of a third party's act -> other. Protagonist and act differ (Denise/switch vs Frank/shove); role structure (harm as means vs side effect) is the manipulation, coded role_change 0.

C-26.note: 'You have not done the reading ... would not be able' -> 'You have done the reading ... prefer not to volunteer': explicit negations removed/changed -> negation_change 1.

C-27.note: Relationship-satisfaction question inserted before the life-satisfaction target in life_second. Insertion, not pure reorder; manipulation_location kept.

C-28.note: Respondent acts as juror about third parties -> mixed_or_third_party (judgment call). 'award' vs 'deny' reframes the same custody outcome as giving vs taking away -> gain_loss 1 (classic Shafir manipulation).

C-29.note: Infers Steve's attitude -> other. One essay sentence changes (continued vs abolished).

C-31.note: Item text identical; the manipulation is the social-identity framing of the respondent ('You are Consumer...other consumers' vs 'You are Individual...other individuals') - coded role_change 1 (identity label of the role changes; structure identical).

C-32.note: Atypical arm adds a 'type 3 reasons why different' prompt before the identical expense question.

C-33.note: Typical arm adds a 'type 3 reasons why similar' prompt.

C-34.note: VN arm adds the IPCC phrase->% table and inserts '(GREATER THAN 90%)' into the very-likely statement. Both arms use a 0-100% scale (explicit probability present regardless). Script negation flags ('unlikely'/'not' from table rows) are artifacts -> negation_change 0.

C-35.note: Same VN table; '(LESS THAN 10%)' inserted into the very-unlikely statement.

C-36.note: Same six K6 items and vague labels in both arms; only item ORDER differs (high-to-low vs low-to-low reversed). Pure reorder -> manipulation_location NaN with na flag. 'Never' option label in both arms -> negation_change 0.

C-37.note: Rates the review's helpfulness (about the reviewer/writer) -> other. Same doctor attributes re-described as positives vs negatives -> gain_loss 1. 'I will always go back' -> 'I will never go back' -> negation_change 1.

C-38.note: Same arm pair as C-37; outcome is trustworthiness of the review writer.
